title: Wealth Building, Investing in People, and Prioritizing Health
summary: In street interviews with wealthy entrepreneurs, including Jesse Itzler, speakers explain how building and selling businesses creates true wealth over time. Itzler shares that getting rich happens slowly, investors bet on hungry people rather than business plans, and maintaining health is the ultimate priority above money.
key_points: How to build real wealth: The first interview subject advises that you do not get rich working for someone else or earning a salary; wealth comes from starting a business, building it for a couple of years, and selling it.
Get rich slowly: Entrepreneur Jesse Itzler, who sold four companies (including to Warren Buffett and Coca-Cola), notes that true wealth creation takes time and occurs slowly.
Earning trajectory: Itzler notes that an entrepreneur will likely make 20 times more money in their 40s than in their 20s.
Invest in people, not just plans: When asked what he looks for in founders, Itzler states 'hunger.' He believes the entrepreneur is the business plan and invests 100% in the person.
Entrepreneurship is not for everyone: Only a small percentage of people are wired for entrepreneurship because it is lonely and carries heavy, real pressure.

Health over wealth: Itzler's core message to the younger generation is to stay healthy, stating that if you have $1 billion but have a sore throat, all you think about is the sore throat. He references the saying: 'If you have health you have hope... You have everything.'

Interviewer: Excuse me sir, sir. I have a question for you. How did you get rich, sir?
Man 1: Yes, sir. Okay. My one piece of advice is this: You don't get rich by working for someone else. You don't get rich by being paid a salary. You get rich by selling your business. So my advice to someone who wants to get rich: start a business, build it up for a couple of years, and then sell it.
Interviewer: What type of company did you sell? Real quick, sir.
Man 1: Are you happy with what I said?
Interviewer: Excuse me, sir. Sir, how did you get rich?
Jesse Itzler: I sold a couple of companies.
Interviewer: How did you get rich?
Jesse Itzler: I sold four companies. One to Warren Buffett, one to Coca-Cola.
Interviewer: How much money did you make? What was the most amount of money you made in a single year?
Jesse Itzler: A lot of money. I worked hard to keep that private.
Interviewer: Could I interview you for a minute? I go all over the world...
Jesse Itzler: I know who you are, man. Come on.
Interviewer: You sold a company to Warren Buffett. What did you learn from doing business with Warren Buffett?
Jesse Itzler: You get rich slowly. It took me a long time. How old are you?
Interviewer: 23.
Jesse Itzler: You'll make 20 times more money in your 40s than you're making now. How much money do you make now? You ask everybody how much money they make. How much money are you making, James? What's the biggest year you've had?
Interviewer: So my business is going to make well over $10 million this year.
Jesse Itzler: At 23?
Interviewer: 23. I promise you.
Jesse Itzler: Can I invest in you now? Wait, you guys are making $10 million a year now?
Interviewer: Over $10 million.
Jesse Itzler: Is it safe to say that your company's probably worth $80 to $100 million now? You want to sell 10% of it?
Interviewer: We could set up a call after this.
Jesse Itzler: No, no, no. Let's do it right now. Let me get my contact... Let's Shark Tank this shit right now.
Interviewer: I'll give you my contact. So what is the number one thing that you look for...
Jesse Itzler: No, let's go back to that, James. I'll give you a check for $10 million today. You talk to your partners, you guys give me 10%. Think about it.
Interviewer: What is the number one thing that you look for in people when you're deciding to invest in them?
Jesse Itzler: Hunger. I see you out there hustling, the way you approached me. You are the business plan.
Interviewer: So you don't invest in businesses, you invest in people.
Jesse Itzler: 100%.
Interviewer: Do you think everybody's built for entrepreneurship?
Jesse Itzler: No.
Interviewer: Why not? What percentage of the population do you think is really cut out for entrepreneurship?
Jesse Itzler: Small. It's lonely being an entrepreneur. The pressure is real, and you have to be able to deal with that. Everybody's not wired like that.
Interviewer: If me and you died tomorrow and you had one more message to the younger generation, what would that be?
Jesse Itzler: At the end of the day, we only have one job, and that's stay healthy. If you have $1 billion and you have a sore throat, every time you swallow, the only thing you think about is your sore throat. And there's an old saying: If you have health, you have hope. You have everything. Stay healthy.
Interviewer: You have amazing advice, sir.
Jesse Itzler: Thank you. Keep doing what you're doing.
